title: Meditating on Scripture
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Meditating on Scripture means prayerfully pondering, treasuring, and dwelling on God’s Word so that it shapes the heart, mind, desires, and obedience. Biblical meditation fills the mind with God’s truth, not emptying the mind from truth.
summary: Meditating on Scripture means prayerfully pondering, treasuring, and dwelling on God’s Word so that it shapes the heart, mind, desires, and obedience. Biblical meditation fills the mind with God’s truth, not emptying the mind from truth.
christFocus: Meditation on Scripture leads believers to deeper communion with Christ. As God’s Word is treasured in the heart, believers learn to abide in Him, trust His promises, obey His commands, and delight in His ways.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture is not only meant to be read quickly and forgotten. God calls His people to dwell on His Word, turn it over in the heart, remember it through the day, and let it shape their thoughts and actions.

Biblical meditation is different from empty reflection or vague spirituality. It is filled with God’s truth. The blessed person delights in the law of the Lord and meditates on it day and night, becoming like a tree planted by streams of water.

Meditation strengthens obedience. God told Joshua to meditate on the Book of the Law so he would be careful to do according to all that was written. Scripture pondered rightly becomes Scripture practiced faithfully.

Meditating on Scripture also redirects the mind. Instead of being ruled by fear, shame, temptation, anger, or anxiety, believers learn to think on what is true, honorable, just, pure, lovely, commendable, excellent, and praiseworthy.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people are constantly meditating without realizing it. They dwell on fear, failure, regret, resentment, temptation, pain, or the opinions of others. What fills the mind eventually shapes the heart.

This doctrine invites believers to let God’s Word become the deep place where their thoughts return. Scripture meditation strengthens weary minds, steadies anxious hearts, and helps believers carry God’s truth into ordinary life.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Choose Scripture to carry with you through the day. Read slowly, repeat it, pray it, ask what it reveals about God, and consider how it calls you to trust and obey. When your mind begins to spiral into fear, temptation, or shame, bring it back to the truth of God’s Word and the hope of Christ.
